reason: This container runs review.sh as a batch job (runs once, exits). HEALTHCHECK is designed for long-running services, not one-shot CLI tools.

Catches LLM knowledge-cutoff false positives for actions/ references where the reviewer asserts 'the latest published major version is vN'. The pattern in global suppressions does not match this phrasing.

Semgrep's python-logger-credential-disclosure rule fires on any logger call whose format string contains words like 'token', 'pricing_file', 'secret', etc. — even when those strings are plain error message templates with no actual credential values. All flagged sites in this repo are informational warning messages, not credential logging.

Semgrep's dangerous-subprocess-use-tainted-env-args rule flags the subprocess.run(args, ...) call in phpstan.py as unsafe because PHPSTAN_LEVEL (an env var) reaches it. Not exploitable: the call uses list-form args with no shell=True, PHPSTAN_LEVEL is validated against _VALID_LEVEL_RE (a single digit, 0-9) before use, and the changed-file paths appended afterward are guarded by an explicit '--' argv separator. An inline `# nosemgrep` comment was tried first (#789 / #790) but was found to be unreliable: Semgrep does not consistently honor it when this file is scanned alongside others, as this repo's own CI does. This rule is the deterministic fallback — it matches on the already-extracted Finding, after Semgrep has run, so it is unaffected by Semgrep's own inline-suppression behavior. Scoped to this exact file+line so a future unsafe subprocess.run added elsewhere in phpstan.py is not silently hidden; if this line number shifts, the suppression stops matching and the finding resurfaces rather than staying hidden.
